title: Raspberry Pi — Blink an LED
summary: The classic first GPIO project. Wire a red LED through a 330 Ω resistor to GPIO17 and ground, then run a 10-line Python script.

steps.instruction: Place the breadboard flat in front of you. Make sure the side with row 1 is on your left.
Push the T-cobbler GPIO breakout into the breadboard so its pins straddle the center gap. The 'GPIO' label should face you.
Connect the ribbon cable from the T-cobbler to the Pi's 40-pin GPIO header. Match the red stripe to pin 1 (next to the SD card slot).
Place the 330 Ω resistor (orange-orange-brown bands) so one leg sits in the same row as the GPIO17 pin, and the other leg crosses to a free row further down.
Insert the LED. The LONG leg (anode, +) goes in the same row as the resistor's far leg. The SHORT leg (cathode, −) goes in a separate row.
Run a jumper from the LED's short leg row to any GND pin on the T-cobbler.
Power on the Pi. On the Pi terminal run: gpio -g mode 17 out && gpio -g write 17 1. The LED should light.
